questions.question: Can you legally block an intersection?

options.text: Yes, if you entered on a green light.
Yes, during rush hour traffic.
No, never.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can cross it completely before the light turns red. Even if the light is green, blocking the intersection is illegal and you can get a ticket.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires slide on water instead of gripping the road. How do you prevent it in the rain?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: In the rain, drive slower. Driving too fast causes your tires to rise up on the water and lose grip with the road. This makes your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: To enter a gap in highway traffic, you should:

options.text: Watch only the cars behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the car ahead.
Speed up and make other cars move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the car ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check the lane you want to enter. Always look to the side and behind your vehicle to make sure no cars are in your way.

questions.question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn at passing cars to get their attention.
Get out and flag down the first car that passes.
Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you stop on an interstate or highway, turn on your emergency flashers and stay inside your vehicle. The high speed of traffic makes standing or walking on an interstate very dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No turning.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction at this location.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
You can pass on the right when it is safe.
You can pass on the left when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline on your side means you can cross it to pass other vehicles from your side of the road.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams bounce back at you, making it harder to see.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must drive through at the posted speed.
The maximum speed limit is 55 mph under good conditions.
You cannot drive slower than 55 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed limit is 55 mph under good conditions.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the maximum speed limit. You can drive slower based on road conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: What should you do before you start driving?

options.text: Recline your seat.
Kick the tires.
Adjust your seat and mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adjust your seat and mirrors.
questions.explanation: Before driving, adjust your seat and mirrors. Have your license and vehicle registration. Make sure all passengers wear seat belts.

questions.question: Why should you look farther ahead on a freeway than on a city street?

options.text: To spot hazards early.
Because it takes a quarter mile to stop your vehicle.
To keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: To spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch for changes in traffic ahead. Watch for signals from other drivers. Be ready for cars merging at on-ramps and expect quick changes in road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: You want to turn right at the corner. A pedestrian with a guide dog is at the corner ready to cross in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off your engine while the person crosses.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross the street.
Wait until the person crosses the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the person crosses the street.
questions.explanation: Always give pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes the right-of-way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Roundabout ahead.
No U-turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Before you change lanes, you should check your mirrors and:

options.text: Never look over your right shoulder.
Always slow down in your traffic lane.
Glance over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Glance over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicles are in your blind spot.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Ease up on the gas pedal.
Brake as hard as possible.
Turn off the ignition.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease up on the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Release the accelerator or brake to regain control. Steer in the direction of the skid.

questions.question: "No zones" are areas around trucks where cars:

options.text: Disappear into blind spots or are so close that the truck driver cannot safely stop or turn.
Have enough space to travel behind the truck.
Have several car lengths between their vehicle and the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Disappear into blind spots or are so close that the truck driver cannot safely stop or turn.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are blind spots around trucks where cars cannot be seen or are too close for the truck driver to maneuver safely.

questions.question: It is unsafe for a child under the age of ____ to ride in the front seat of a car.
questions.explanation: Children under 13 should sit in the back seat with a seatbelt or car seat for safety.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks entering.
Truck exit only.
Steep downgrade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep hill is ahead. Check your brakes before driving down.

questions.question: Why is it more dangerous to drive at night than during the day?

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
The road is always more slippery at night.
Your reaction time is slower at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
questions.explanation: At night, you have less visibility and oncoming headlights cause glare. Always use headlights and drive carefully in the dark.

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and slow down to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up and smoothly merge with traffic on the interstate. Do not stop.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, you should:

options.text: Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.
Pump the brakes rapidly.
Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tight and take your foot off the gas. Let the car slow down naturally. Gently apply brakes once the vehicle has slowed.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Drive faster to avoid causing an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: When driving in fog, slow down and use your low beam lights. If fog is too thick and you cannot see, pull over and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in rain or fog?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. They help other drivers see you, even if they don't help you see much better.

questions.question: What should you do when a traffic light is not working?

options.text: Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.
You do not need to stop if the intersection is clear.
Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection as an all-way stop. Come to a complete stop, look both ways, and yield the right-of-way before entering.

questions.question: When using a deceleration lane to exit, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use your turn signal until you are in the deceleration lane.
Do not follow posted speeds unless the road is slippery.
Do not slow down until you are in the deceleration lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not slow down until you are in the deceleration lane.
questions.explanation: Stay at a safe speed and do not slow down before entering the deceleration lane. Once in the lane, slow down gradually until you reach the posted speed for the ramp.

questions.question: Which road surface freezes first?

options.text: A tunnel
An intersection
A bridge

questions.correctAnswerText: A bridge
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other roads because they are exposed to cold air on both sides. Bridges freeze first and thaw last.
